title: Shopify Mailchimp Integration: Setup Guide (2026)
summary: Shopify Mailchimp integration connects new customers to your email list automatically. Understand the workflow needed and which no-code tools support this.
body_markdown:
## The new customer Mailchimp workflow


This flow doesn't need a custom step: a Shopify "New Customer" trigger feeds a Mailchimp "Add or Update Subscriber" action, with email, name and status mapped, then tested and published.


### Stage 1: Shopify trigger and store connection


Pick Shopify as the trigger app and choose "New Customer". Then connect your store, which opens a Shopify authorization dialog.


Approve it while logged into the right store. If you manage several, a wrong login here connects the wrong shop, and the flow will run happily against it.


Once connected, pull a sample customer. If the sample comes back empty, create a test customer first.


### Stage 2: Mailchimp action and audience


Add Mailchimp as the action and choose "Add or Update Subscriber". "Update" matters: a returning customer who already exists in the audience is changed, not duplicated and not rejected.


Connect your Mailchimp account through its own authorization dialog, then select the audience. A Mailchimp account can hold more than one, and the dropdown won't warn you if you pick the wrong one.


### Mapping Shopify fields and consent status in Mailchimp


Map the email address first. It's the identifier Mailchimp uses to decide whether a subscriber is new or existing. Then map first and last name from the Shopify customer fields.


Slow down on status. **Don't hardcode "subscribed" for everyone.** A new customer has bought something, which isn't the same as agreeing to marketing email.


Map status from the customer's marketing consent where the sample data exposes it. If you want a confirmation email sent first, use "pending", which makes Mailchimp ask for double opt-in.


> ** A new customer has bought something, which isn't the same as agreeing to marketing email.


### Testing and publishing the Mailchimp automation


Run the test with the sample customer from Stage 1. Then open the Mailchimp audience and confirm the contact is there with the right name and status.


When the test run goes green, all it means is that the action finished. The audience tells you it did the right thing. Fix any mismatch in the mapping, rerun, and publish only when the contact looks correct.


Activepieces gives you something to hold that audience up against.


Describe this flow in its built-in chat, a Shopify "New Customer" trigger into Mailchimp "Add or Update Subscriber", and what it publishes is a live flow in your account with the same four stages you would have assembled by hand, plus a run trace showing exactly what each step did with the sample customer.


Anyone on the team can read that trace without a certification, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production with those traces sitting under the same RBAC and audit logs as every other flow there.
